options.text: $\phi$ is monotonic increasing in $\left[0, \frac{1}{2}\right]$ and monotonic decrasing in $\left[\frac{1}{2}, 1\right]$
$\phi$ is monotonic increasing in $\left[\frac{1}{2}, 1\right]$ and monotonic decrasing in $\left[0, \frac{1}{2}\right]$
$\phi$ is neither increasing nor decreasing in any sub interval of $[0,1]$

solution.text:
Hint:
$\phi^{\prime}(x)=f^{\prime}(x)-f^{\prime}(1-x)$
$f^{\prime}(x)-f^{\prime}(1-x) \geq 0$ (for monotonic increasing)
$f^{\prime}(x) \geq f^{\prime}(1-x), x \leq 1-x\left(\because f^{\prime}(x)\right.$ is decreasing)
$\mathrm{x} \leq \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \phi(\mathrm{x})$ is monotonic increasing in $\left[0, \frac{1}{2}\right]$ and monotonic decreasing in $\left[\frac{1}{2}, 1\right]$
